about.title: Salinas Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Salinas moves on a handful of arterials, and that is where most of the city's collisions show up in the public record. N Main Street, E Market Street, E Laurel Drive and E Boronda Road carry the highest counts, and reports cluster on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m., when the workday lets out and weekend traffic joins the same lanes. In 2025, the most recent final year on record, Salinas logged 410 injury collisions that left 560 people hurt and one person dead. Behind each of those numbers is somebody trying to figure out what comes next. If that is you, LawProactive can connect you at no cost with an independent attorney who handles car accident claims in Monterey County. You do not pay us anything, and the attorney works on contingency, so there is no fee unless your case produces a recovery. The sooner evidence like dashcam footage, photos and witness names is preserved, the more options you tend to have.

items.title: California's two-year clock is shorter than it sounds
items.desc: Most car accident claims must be filed within two years, but if a city or county vehicle was involved, the window to file a government claim can be as short as six months. Connecting early keeps those deadlines from quietly closing.

items.title: Partial fault does not end your claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you carried some of the blame for a crash on E Market Street; your share simply reduces the amount. An attorney can push back when an insurer tries to inflate your percentage.

items.title: No cap on pain and suffering, and no fee up front
items.desc: California places no statutory limit on non-economic damages in a standard car accident case. The attorneys in our network work on contingency, so you owe nothing unless there is a recovery.

items.question: The other driver's insurance adjuster called me the day after my crash on E Laurel Drive. Should I give a recorded statement?
items.answer: You are not required to give the other side's insurer a recorded statement, and it is usually wise to decline until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used later to shift fault onto you. You can simply say you are not ready to discuss the details and let them know an attorney will follow up.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge me anything to be connected with an attorney?
items.answer: No. Our connection service is free, and we are not a law firm. The independent attorney you are matched with works on a contingency fee, meaning payment comes out of any recovery rather than your pocket, and if there is no recovery there is no fee.

items.question: What should I save after a Salinas car accident?
items.answer: Hold on to photos of the vehicles, the scene and your injuries, plus the police report number and contact details for any witnesses. Keep every medical bill, prescription receipt and note about missed work. If a nearby business or a dashcam may have caught the crash, mention it right away, since that footage is often overwritten within days.
